If values.get(option) is null or empty, the method falls back to the defaultValues parameter, so another test should leave the option unset and verify the passed-in default list is returned. Beyond that, if the parameter default is also null or empty, it falls to the internal defaultValues map for that option, and finally defaults to an empty list if nothing else applies -- I need tests covering each of these fallback tiers.

Passing an empty ArrayList as the defaultValues param hits this isEmpty()-true branch since valueList gets reassigned to that empty param, triggering the fallback to the default map. To also hit the first condition's isEmpty() branch, I'd need values.get(option) itself to return an empty (non-null) list.

Since addValue always inserts an element right after creating that list, the stored list can never remain empty through public API calls, so that first isEmpty() branch looks unreachable in normal usage — I'll flag this as a minor design note rather than a real fault, then move on to testing the case where the option is missing entirely from defaultValues so the lookup returns null and falls through to the final EMPTY_LIST assignment.
